subject: Completely independent scales when using facet_grid

messages.author: 6d1cd0a71e6148df
messages.subject: Completely independent scales when using facet_grid
parts:
Dear list members,

Is it possible to get *really* free scales when using facet_grid,
i.e., where the scales of each panel are *completely* independent from
each other? Here’s a simple example:

#####
library(ggplot2)

n = 40
d = data.frame(cat1=rep(1:3, each=n), cat2=rep(4:6, times=n))
d$x = .5*rnorm(3*n) + 3*d$cat1
d$y = 2*d$x + .5*rnorm(3*n) + 3*d$cat2
d$cat1 = LETTERS[d$cat1]
d$cat2 = letters[d$cat2]

qplot(x, y, data=d) + facet_grid(cat1~cat2)
qplot(x, y, data=d) + facet_grid(cat1~cat2, scales="free")
#####

The scales for each row and for each column differ, but within a row
the y scales are identical, and within in column the x scales are
identical. What I want is basically this:

#####
qplot(x, y, data=d) + facet_wrap(cat1~cat2, scales="free")
#####

But this wastes a lot of space because the panel strips are repeated
for each panel, instead of once for each row and column. But note that
I *want* the *axis labels* to be repeated for each panel, since the
actual x and y values do matter (so I can’t just rescale my data).

Also, the facet_wrap trick won’t work when not all combinations for
values are present, like here:

#####
d = subset(d, !(cat1 == "B" & cat2 == "e"))
#####

One solution is to use ‘lattice’, which supports completely
independent scales for panels, but I’d rather stay with ‘ggplot2’.
Here’s the ‘lattice’ solution (which would work better if the
horizontal strips where on the right, BTW):

#####
library(latticeExtra)
p = xyplot(y~x | cat1+cat2, data=d, scales=list(relation="free"))
useOuterStrips(p)
#####

Is there a way of accomplishing the same thing in ‘ggplot2’?

--
Karl Ove Hufthammer
